en: Therīgāthā 6.2 Chakkanipāta Vāseṭṭhītherīgāthā The Verses of the Elder Nun Vāseṭṭhī, from the Sixth Chapter (The Group of Six) I was born into a wealthy family; my father was rich and possessed of great wealth. My mother was named Bhaddā, and my name was Vāseṭṭhī. I was beautiful, fair-skinned, and charming; I was well-versed in the arts and skilled in dance. I was honored by many people, and I delighted in the pleasures of the senses. Then, seeing the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, I went forth into homelessness under the Dhamma of the Well-Gone One. Having gone forth, I am now free from all bonds; I have attained the destruction of craving. I am a nun who has reached the goal, cooled and with taints destroyed. I remember my former birth; I was once a courtesan in Benares. I was honored by many people, and I delighted in the pleasures of the senses. But when I saw the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, I went forth into homelessness under the Dhamma of the Well-Gone One. “Afflicted by grief for my son,
my mind distracted and my senses clouded,
I am naked with my hair disheveled.”
Wandering here and there through streets, heaps of refuse,
cemeteries, and roads.
I practiced for three years,
afflicted by hunger and thirst.
Then I saw the Sugata.
Toward the city of Mithilā, [he went] to the Fully Awakened One,
the tamer of the untamed,
who is fearless from every quarter.
Having regained my own mind and paid homage, I approached him;
he taught the Dhamma to me.
Out of compassion, Gotama [taught him].
Having heard his Dhamma,
I went forth into the homeless life.
Applying myself to the words of the Teacher,
I realized the auspicious state.
All sorrows have been utterly severed.
These have been abandoned, and this is their end;
for the bases from which sorrow arises have been fully understood by me.
… the Elder Nun Vāseṭṭhī …
